Monthly Newsletters

October 2026

  • Posit Conf 2026 took place in October. From the times when it was RStudio Conf, it happened to become the major global R syncing event. Now is a good moment to catch up on announcements and talks. https://lnkd.in/p/eEYfAN9a
  • The R ecosystem saw an explosion of package & environment managers in the last years: {renv}, {}rix}, rv, uvr and ir – just to name the most notable ones. Isabella Velásquez overviewed them in a nice systemizing blog post https://rworks.dev/posts/r-managers
  • Polars 2.0 is out. The Rust-based dataframe library hits a major milestone. Curiously (and this links to our previous talk in {qqsl}), one of the major news is that now SQL is a first-class citizen on this hype train https://pola.rs/posts/release-polars-2
  • Some (regular, already) magic from James Balamuta – turn an R project into a standalone website that runs R, serverless. {webrarian} packs an R project so the analysis runs live in the browser — no server needed. https://lnkd.in/p/e4X9XBNK
  • Quarto is being rebuilt in Rust. So far, this is an experimental Quarto 2 (q2) implementation, but this is likely an early signal of where publishing tooling is heading – towards even faster and more reliable execution https://lnkd.in/p/e9ebVZez
  • I thought I would never stop recommending the Hard Fork podcast. And I won’t. Only, the original hosts are moving to create their own new podcast called Machine Gods, to be launched on 19th October. At the same time, Hard Fork continues at NYT with new hosts, and it’s also good. But I heartily encourage you to follow the new show of Kevin Roos and Casey Newton – I find it being the single most useful source in attempts to digest the ongoing tsunami of AI related news. I’m linking Casey’s final reflection on Hard Fork and the transition to independent Machine Gods podcast https://www.platformer.news/hard-fork-machine-gods/?ref=platformer-newsletter

September 2026

  • Our special 4R/um meeting & R Meetup Copengagen event is moved to Friday 23th October 2026 at 14:00 [NOTE unusual time!] due to an overlap with we are joining forces with Rasmus Bååth, the organizer of CopenhagenR useR Group via Meetup. We are going to have 3 ~20min presentations, 2 from guest speakers and 1 from an internal DST speaker.
  • Posit rolled out an Introduction course for Positron IDE – https://academy.posit.co/path/introduction-to-positron
  • A no bullshit guide to LLMs – Hadley Wickham summarized many battle learned lessons about using AI with coding https://tidydesign.substack.com/p/a-no-bullshit-guide-to-llms
  • R Observatory – James Balamuta created a really neat resource to explore package docs https://blog.thecoatlessprofessor.com/posts/beginnings-of-the-r-observatory-project
  • {uvr} is here to bring the best of python’s wotrld pacjage management to R https://www.linkedin.com/posts/veerlevanleemput_you-probably-heard-about-uv-for-python-share-7487847611631046656-ijTA
  • This one is honestly a bit mind-blowing: share a bit of R code as a live executable R session with {livelink}, another masterpiece from James Balamuta https://blog.thecoatlessprofessor.com/programming/r/data-science-as-a-reproducible-link OR at least just check webR demo https://webr.sh

June 2026

  • On Tuesday 25th August 2026 at 14:00 [NOTE unusual day/time!], we are going to have a special 4R/um meeting – we are joining forces with Rasmus Bååth, the organizer of CopenhagenR useR Group via Meetup. We are going to have 3 ~20min presentations, 2 from guest speakers and 1 from an internal DST speaker. More info will follow after summer
  • REMINDER: On 25th September 2026 we are going to have a very special guest at 4R/um – Thomas Lin Pedersen, one of the most influential R developers who works at Posit, the author of {ggforce}, {patchwork}, {ragg}, {ggraph}, {ggfx}, the redefined {gganimate}, maintainer and lead developer of {ggplot2}, and many many more great packages. He will present his latest major pivot – {ggsql}. Please mark in your calendars, come, and bring your non-R colleague who works with SQL – https://ggsql.org
  • Hadley Wickham announced getting back to his Substack blog. And of course you can see that the dominating topic is the ongoing AI revolution.
  • {tidypredict} is a package of the established tidymodels family that follows the idea of SQL revival and enablement. It allows fitting statistical models directly on the database – https://tidypredict.tidymodels.org/

May 2026

  • Lean R 4.6.0 installation is live and flying – try it, you would really feel the speed boost, clearly visible even from the startup time, packages panel is usable, autocomplete is not lagging =)
  • On 25th September 2026 we are going to have a very special guest at 4R/um – Thomas Lin Pedersen, one of the most influential R developers who works at Posit, the author of {ggforce}, {patchwork}, {ragg}, {ggraph}, {ggfx}, the redefined {gganimate}, maintainer and lead developer of {ggplot2}, and many many more great packages. He will present his latest major pivot – {ggsql}. Please mark in your calendars, come, and bring your non-R colleague who works with SQL – https://ggsql.org
  • Another internal news. On 8, 9, and 12 June at 9:00–12:00 I will be teaching Dataviz with R course. [Note: 3 days instead of 5 claimed in the initial dstalle email] Apparently, I overestimated the demand for the course, and we are not at risk of not fitting in the room =) this means that you may safely plan to attend one, two, or all three of the workshop days. The three days are planned as follows: 1) basic dataviz principles & recap of tidyverse; 2) intro to ggplot2 and a deeper dive into ggplot2 specific useful plot types; 3) maps in R + interactivity. Please feel free to join any of the days but do write to me (ikx@dst.dk) at least a day in advance so that I can properly plan the workshops. More info on the course and all the R scripts are here – https://github.com/ikashnitsky/dataviz-art-skill
  • A balanced, thoughtful, well-argumented essay on the tradeoffs of choosing R/py vs SAS in pharma, a highly regulated industry with deep roots in SAS usage. The difference of official statistics from phara is only in the level of consolidated collaborative effort in building and maintaining open-source ecosystem – https://www.appsilon.com/post/r-python-sas-modern-sce-comparison + one example of SAS v R in production
  • Typst is maturing into a powerful document authoring engine with a first-class support in Quarto – https://www.linkedin.com/posts/veerlevanleemput_lots-been-going-on-around-typst-lately-new-share-7457388222441062400-tRVe
  • Andrey Karpathy’s fresh take on creating and maintaining an AI-driven knowledge base as a wiki of simple .md files caught the industry by surprise with it’s simplicity and power. Here is an R package {pensar} that implements the approach in our most cozy environment – https://cran.r-project.org/package=pensar
  • You may have noticed that every newsletter features something to do with duckdb, the surprising disrupting technology in bigdata heavy-load computing. (Just have a look at this illuminating blog post). One field where the benefits of blazing fast processing are most notable is spatial analysis. And here comes the stable 1.0.0 release of the framework package {duckspatial} – https://www.linkedin.com/posts/adrian-cidre_duckspatial-v100-is-now-on-cran-ugcPost-7444462268743966720-_jRL
  • The concept of skills.md for AI agents becomes a dominant field of tuning agentic AI systems to work productively and predictably. Look at the collection of skills tailors specifically for R – https://www.linkedin.com/posts/david-underwood-416a4513_a-few-claude-skills-for-r-users-r-works-share-7455232673876430850-2-nn + for {tidymodels} https://skills.tidymodels.org/
  • Surely you’ve heard multiple times the claims that “AI will soon take our jobs”, probably often enough to dismiss it as fearmongering. The key word here is “our”. And the key question that likely worries everyone is: Will it soon grab my job? What’s really happening in job displacement today? Here’s he single most useful AI job revolution explainer https://sequoiacap.com/article/services-the-new-software
  • Addy Osmani, head of Google Cloud AI team, wrote a beautiful essay on the distinction between letting AI helpers strengthen one’s working ability vs allowing it to displace yourself. He introduces a useful concept of “cognitive surrender” a provides a set of actionable tips how to make sure that AI helps you develop/grow – https://addyosmani.com/blog/cognitive-surrender
  • Another great essay on the related topic – From technical debt to cognitive debt – https://margaretstorey.com/blog/2026/02/09/cognitive-debt
  • AI coding agents/helpers have already redefined the programming world. Here is a recent real-world example that is nice to have at hand the next time someone would recycle the “stochastic parrots” argument staright back from 2023 – https://www.linkedin.com/posts/kirill-balakhonov_to-me-this-is-the-most-epic-coding-ai-story-ugcPost-7460692232183025665-fRYh
  • This is a fun one. Imagine you traveled in 1930 and can ask the people of that time whatever. You have a chance with Talkie, a research project that trained an LLM only based on data before 1930 – https://talkie-lm.com/introducing-talkie (listen to the researcher who develops the project in last week’s Hard Fork episode)

April 2026

  • R 4.6.0 is scheduled to be released on 24th April 2026. Once we have it in house (probably in mid-May) we are going to introduce a big improvement with a whitelist of selected packages that should cover most the everyday needs. Not having the whole of CRAN installed by default would make the Packages pane usable and the overall performance of RStudio much smoother. There will soon be a separate email on the matter specifically. Some news about R 4.6.0 – https://www.jumpingrivers.com/blog/whats-new-r46
  • Quarto 1.9 got released and this is a pretty big update. But the developers of Quarto published their views about the upcoming major update to the 2.0 version in about half a year. This is going to phenomenal – https://quarto.org/docs/blog/posts/2026-04-06-whats-next-quarto-2
  • Yet another brief explainer from the developer of Positron on why this is a unique coding environment aimed at data scientists – https://www.linkedin.com/posts/your-tools-shape-your-thinking-thats-the-ugcPost-7447277532787314688-YFGK
  • For decades the core developers of R were answering questions and helping to troubleshoot issues via R mailing lists. This throve of useful knowledge used to be hardly accessible. No more. Check out – https://r-mailing-lists.thecoatlessprofessor.com/
  • You probably saw the news that Posit launched their own AI service now available in RStudio (alas, subscription based). Here is a screencast from Hadley Wickham showcasing the power of this new tool to explore a dataset – https://youtu.be/N_oT_8xVRXg?si=4NzZO-kHSiPs9PWI (and just a reminder that in Posit you can have AI assistants without a Posit AI subscription)
  • Databot – Following the previous bullet point, here’s a new Positron/VScode extension specifically focused on helping you to explore datasets – https://open-vsx.org/extension/posit/databot
  • Yet another package from the amazing Posit team. {pointblank} is a powerful workhorse to automate exploration and validation of datasets. This one may turn out to be invaluable for us at DST – https://github.com/rstudio/pointblank
  • Some of the best R developers are working for pharma companies that completely converted to R. Pharmaverse is really a thing to explore. Here is one small but powerful example – https://pharmaverse.github.io/blog/posts/2026-03-29-meet-dataviewr-the/meet-dataviewr-the-view-you-always-wanted.html
  • A beautiful post on the importance of reproducibility by Sara Weston – https://www.linkedin.com/posts/sara-weston-phd_early-in-my-postdoc-i-built-an-analysis-share-7444944983415197697--1mO
  • April saw a breakthrough in locally run AI models – the release of Google’s Gemma 4 open source family of models. They are compact enough to be run on laptops and even top smartphones and powerful enough to be actually useful in agentic AI orchestration. Here’s an opinion from a brilliant R developer Kyle Walker – https://www.linkedin.com/posts/walkerke_all-the-hype-is-around-what-anthropic-openai-share-7450161870642094080-zC0T
  • AI systems are relentless. And this is not only good. Basically, they structurally have no concept of “good enough”. And this is one reason why they need a human, lazy and mortal, wishing to finalize this damn project “before weekend” to keep them in check. A brilliant essay by Bryan Cantrill – https://bcantrill.dtrace.org/2026/04/12/the-peril-of-laziness-lost

March 2026

  • With the recent {dplyr} major update, if_else() and case_when() are up to 30x faster — a dedicated post explains the memory and speed engineering behind the dplyr 1.2.0 gains – https://tidyverse.org/blog/2026/02/dplyr-case-when-faster
  • RStudio rolled out its own AI coding agent. Unfortunately, it’s a paid plan with 14 days trial. But this may be transformative for those not switching to Positron/VSCode https://posit.co/blog/introducing-ai-in-rstudio
  • Tad – an extremely capable small app to view CSV, parquet, duckdb, and SQLite. Open source, cross platform, fast, clean. I didn’t flinch at my request to open a 1 million rows 500MB csv file. But that’s not all: it can blazingly fast create pivot tables to explore your data – https://github.com/antonycourtney/tad
  • Quarto v1.9 – a fresh Quarto release lands with notable Typst improvements. Typst is a new generation tool to compile PDFs that unlike LaTeX manages in seconds rather than minutes – https://quarto.org/docs/blog
  • {webRoid} and {webRios} – two packages that allow you to run R right on you mobile phone. Yes, I know this is likely not for everyone =) but this is great option to have, especially since Android is drifting toward becoming a fully fleshed desktop OS. Did you know you can connect to a DST virtual machine via Android Microsoft app then plug the phone to you docking station and just work? – https://www.linkedin.com/posts/steven-mortimer_rstats-webroid-webrios-activity-7419714410864199680-9n2X
  • {ragnar} 0.3.0 — the tidyverse’s RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) package keeps evolving: faster document ingestion, new embedding providers, improved retrieval, and new integrations for using ragnar stores directly from tool calls in LLM agents – https://tidyverse.org/blog/2026/01/ragnar-0-3-0
  • {orbital} – a new development in the world of data science led by Posit – translate model creation from R or python to bare SQL and train the models right at the database. This one is just to observe and follow https://www.linkedin.com/posts/hadleywickham_orbital-is-a-such-tool-technology-build-share-7438300413973651456-RFpz
  • Posit evaluation of small AI coding models – https://www.linkedin.com/posts/simonpcouch_i-had-wondered-how-todays-gpt-54-releases-share-7439764257778409472-A9-F
  • A great discussion of how AI coding redefined the unspoken agreement between the actors in the Opensouce world – https://turso.tech/blog/what-happens-with-oss-in-the-age-of-ai

February 2026

  • {labelled} – I came across this fantastic suggestion, one can simply specify how the data variables should appear in the plots, and this info will be carried on into the outputs. Think of using this for labelles in Danish that you only need to define once – https://www.linkedin.com/posts/cameron-patrick-5b348013b_was-recently-reminded-of-a-cool-r-trick-activity-7423346487193153536-ltiJ
  • {dplyr}, the workhorse of tidy R scripting got a large upgrade with handy new functions and a speed boost to some old ones – https://tidyverse.org/blog/2026/02/dplyr-1-2-0
  • {FakeDataR} – often we can’t share the sensitive data. One option is to generate a synthetic dataset that would preserve the main statistical features of the original dataset. Explore – https://www.linkedin.com/posts/zobaer-ahmed_rstats-cran-llm-activity-7381524554655039488-TwCf
  • Quarto Wizard – navigating the endless possibilities of Quarto becomes easier and more straightforward with a VS Code extension – https://quarto.org/docs/blog/posts/2025-10-20-quarto-wizard-1-0-0
  • The transition from RStudio to Positron has lots of quirks. Andrew Heiss recently showcased many handy tools that helped him modernize his workflows – https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7429906310151970816
  • R is akin smoking – if you sometimes think that R is tough and weird, have a look at the comparison people had before tidy era https://www.johndcook.com/blog/2012/02/29/comparing-r-to-smoking 
  • Hard Fork — not just R, but extremely relevant to anyone trying to stay synced with the development of technology. It’s a podcast run by two prominent journalists. For example, the last episode discussed not the future but already the lived reality where AI agents write all of the code previously designed and typed in by humans, and how this changes the landscape of programming. Check the podcast on any streaming platform, including YouTube where sometimes the video is also useful 

October 2025

  • https://www.tidyverse.org/blog/2025/09/ggplot2-4-0-0 – the main R dataviz framework package got a large update + https://www.linkedin.com/posts/veerlevanleemput_in-june-ggplot2-had-its-18th-birthday-activity-7372203806425661440-OImM + https://bsky.app/profile/andrew.heiss.phd/post/3m2acbz6lbk2z
  • https://www.linkedin.com/posts/yan-holtz-2477534a_beginner-or-intermediate-r-user-this-activity-7369347689521606658-0_bj – best practice in R cheat sheet
  • https://www.linkedin.com/posts/walkerke_take-the-time-to-learn-the-mirai-package-activity-7371545592759701504-cwme – async computing is a powerful framework for dealing with heavy computations; and with {mirai} they become first class citizens in the tidyverse
  • https://www.linkedin.com/posts/adam-kucharski-1a1b0225b_if-youre-writing-a-grant-and-have-to-create-activity-7370931708994539520-DMTj – Gantt plots are useful for project management
  • https://jcarroll.com.au/2025/09/13/i-vibe-coded-an-r-package – LLMs are here to stay; it’s worth checking how experienced R developers may leverage the power of LLMs for developing R packages
  • https://cols4all.github.io/cols4all-R – amazing package to choose colours; this one is probable now the most powerful framework for dealing with colour palettes in R
  • https://www.linkedin.com/posts/sharonmachlis_presentation-ready-data-summary-and-analytic-activity-7381842453802151936-NQ9v – {gtsummary} summarizes data sets, regression models, and more, using sensible defaults with highly customizable capabilities

September 2025

  • https://hadley.github.io/25-tidyverse-history – Hadley Wickham is for sure the most influential developer in R world. In his recent long interview he reflects on his professional path and the development of tidyverse
  • https://r-consortium.org/posts/r_plus_ai_call_for_proposals/index.html#rai-november-12-13-2025 – there will be a curious online conference, 12–13 November 2025, organized by R Consortium to discuss AI developments in R ecosystem. Until 5th September 2025, you can propose topics to be discussed there.
  • https://ces0491.github.io/rbr – A beautiful book was published in summer by Cesaire Tobias that is aimed at the heavy users of R who may have missed some crucial training in the basics of proper computer science workflows and environment setup
  • https://www.tidyverse.org/blog/2025/07/purrr-1-1-0-parallel – recently a huge update happened to {purrr} that introduced a drop=in zero-cost parallelization in main tidyverse pipelines
  • https://positron.posit.co/release-notes.html – after more than a year in Beta testing, Positron (a new VS Code based IDE from Posit, focused on data analysis in python and R) is now fully released
  • https://www.linkedin.com/posts/jakub-sobolewski-r_rstats-rdevelopment-opensource-activity-7348682381156913154-8rv4 – since some of us at DST are developing/maintaining own R packages, I wanted to share this post on the modern tools for code coverage and testing
  • https://luisdva.github.io/llmsr-book – for anyone interested in learning how LLMs may be utilised in R, this constantly updated book is a gem
